subject: Clarify: where Medisys requests execute, temporary storage, and erase responsibility
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@medisys.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.example.com, security@redwood.example.com
Cc: legal@medisys.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where Medisys traffic runs and what gets persisted?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — impressed with the latency numbers. Before we move to a pilot, our SecOps and Legal teams have a few concrete questions about runtime geography and deletion accountability so we can complete our vendor assessment. Can you confirm the following for requests routed through Redwood Hosted API (no Dedicated pool for this pilot):

1) Where are inference requests executed (region/hop-level): are there intermediate hops outside the US?
2) Does Redwood persist request payloads, intermediate KV cache, or embeddings beyond the request lifecycle? If so, where (which region) and for how long?
3) Which subprocessors/processes could temporarily touch request payloads (e.g., logging, telemetry, GPU cloud providers, analytics)? We need current inventory and contract flow-down assurances.
4) If Medisys asks for deletion/erasure, who is the accountable party for erasing transient caches and any logs? How fast is the erase path?

We need short, evidence-backed answers (screenshots, architecture diagram, or a CSV of subprocessor endpoints are helpful). Target turnaround: EOD PDT today if possible.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Security & Compliance
Medisys Health

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where Medisys traffic runs and what gets persisted?

Sara — thanks for the precise list. Short answers up front; more detail below and an evidence pack attached.

1) Execution loci: Primary execution for Hosted API customers in the us region occurs in us-west-2 and us-east-1 (AWS). Host-level routing prefers same-region execution; on rare capacity events, requests may failover to a nearest compatible US region only. No routine hops to APAC/EU for a US-scoped account. We do not route through third-country caches by default.

2) Persistence: By default Redwood treats inference payloads as ephemeral: request payloads and KV caches are kept in-memory during the session and are not written to durable object storage. Transient telemetry (summaries/metrics) is reported to a central telemetry pipeline with PII-stripping rules. Long-lived artifacts (embeddings, evaluations) are only retained when explicitly enabled by the customer via API or Console and are stored in the region the customer selects (for Medisys pilot you can opt-in to US-only storage). Default retention for telemetry logs is 30 days (audit-level), with an option to shorten.

3) Subprocessors: Short inventory: AWS (us-west-2/us-east-1), Prometheus/Datadog (metrics aggregation), Sentry (error traces), and our managed GKE partners for some Dedicated offering workflows. For Hosted inference these subprocessors handle telemetry and control-plane metadata only; inference compute runs on AWS EC2/GPU instances. Contracts include flow-down security clauses and SOC2 evidence; see attachment subprocessor-inventory-2028-06.csv.

4) Erasure accountability: Redwood is responsible for erasing transient runtime caches and platform telemetry under our standard customer data deletion SLA; the customer is responsible for data they intentionally store (embeddings, persisted prompts). Deletion request flow: 1) Customer submits deletion request via Console or Support ticket -> 2) Automation triggers immediate in-memory KV eviction and marks related telemetry for expedited purge -> 3) Background job reconciles and deletes any persisted diagnostic logs within 72 hours. We provide a deletion report with timestamps and cloud tenant identifiers.

I attached a lightweight execution map and the subprocessor inventory CSV. Marissa and Connor are looped in for any follow-ups or formal evidence pack exports. If you want a signed attestation for the pilot, we can escalate to Legal.

Best,

Looping in a brief ops note / internal checklist for the deletion SLA in case Medisys presses on timing:

- Confirm account is US-region-scoped in our control plane (we did when provisioning).
- Verify telemetry retention override: set to 7 days for the pilot (Ops can do).
- On deletion ticket: tag as MED-2387-delete -> run automated in-memory eviction -> launch cloud-native log purge (CloudWatch) with expedited flag.
- Generate deletion report CSV (includes request-id, cloud-region, node-ids) and attach to HubSpot record.

Connor: can you pull last 90-day subprocessor access logs and attach one sample request-id trace for evidence? I want to include a sample cloudwatch-event with node id and timestamp.
